description: Vessim is the Distributed and Operating Systems research group's Python testbed for microgrid and energy-aware computing simulations. It combines loads, generation, storage and grid exchange, with controllers, historical traces and optional real software or hardware in the loop. Inputs are component settings, time series and control policies; outputs include energy-system states and logged performance over a selected period. Coverage ranges from local devices to configured data-centre systems, not a fixed geographic dataset. Public source is free under MIT, with an optional software-in-the-loop extension. A limitation is that component fidelity and timing depend on the chosen simulators, while live integrations require separately configured services. The included battery example is a simplified model. Vessim can test dispatch, outage response and carbon-aware computing, complementing PyPSA (model-pypsa) for energy-system planning. The README supplies an executable example and cites its testbed and co-simulation papers. No Prometheus service, live hardware or trace dataset was accessed.
